title: Build a SQL IN clause and a name list with joining

blocks.text: `Collectors.joining(delimiter, prefix, suffix)` concatenates a stream of strings through one `StringBuilder`, with the delimiter only *between* elements and the prefix and suffix around the whole result.

items: `String inClause(List<Integer> ids)`: the ids in list order, separated by `", "`, inside parentheses.
`String nameList(List<String> names)`: the names that are not blank, in list order, separated by `", "`, inside square brackets.

blocks.text: Consider an empty id list, and names that are empty or only spaces.

cases.says: It joins the ids into an IN clause and the names into a bracketed list.
An empty id list gives "()": joining still writes its prefix and suffix.
Blank names are filtered out before joining, so no empty slot appears between delimiters.

concepts: joining writes its delimiter only between elements and its prefix and suffix even around nothing.
